This page publishes the **current public install sequence** for
[UpstreamDrift](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift). Commands and
prerequisites are copied from the upstream
[README](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/625a16e6897b88ab29fb5a64c65ecee820dd58f5/README.md)
at commit `625a16e6897b` (2026-11-11). UpstreamDrift remains the live authority;
AffineDrift CI re-checks this page against
`data/upstreamdrift/install_readme_contract.json`.

For scriptable runs without the GUI, see [Headless Simulation and Agent Use](upstreamdrift-headless-and-agents.html).

## Prerequisites

- **Python 3.11 or 3.12.** UpstreamDrift declares `requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.13"` in
  `pyproject.toml` at the cited commit.
- **Git.** The shared Tools layer at `vendor/ud-tools` is a **mandatory** submodule;
  the platform will not import without it. The repository **does not use Git LFS**.
- **MATLAB R2023a or later** with Simulink and Simscape Multibody — only if you use the
  historical MATLAB models, not for the Python platform alone.

## Standard Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift.git
cd UpstreamDrift
git submodule update --init --recursive vendor/ud-tools

pip install -e ".[dev]"

python scripts/ci/verify_installation.py
```

Only `vendor/ud-tools` is required. Model submodules (`opensim-models`, `myo_sim`,
`human-gazebo`) are optional and needed only for experimental OpenSim or MyoSuite work.

## Launch the Platform

```bash
python launch_upstream_drift.py
```

This starts the local API server on port 8000 and opens the web interface. Common
variants from the README:

| Command | Opens |
| --- | --- |
| `python launch_upstream_drift.py` | Web interface (default) |
| `python launch_upstream_drift.py --classic` | PyQt6 desktop application |
| `python launch_upstream_drift.py --api-only` | API server without a UI |
| `upstream-drift` | Same as `launch_upstream_drift.py` (console script) |

## Mock Engine (Interface Development Only)

To work on UI or API plumbing without loading a physics engine:

```bash
pip install -e .
export GOLF_USE_MOCK_ENGINE=1
```

Output is synthetic. Do not treat it as a physics result.

## Troubleshooting

If installation fails, follow the upstream
[installation troubleshooting](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/625a16e6897b88ab29fb5a64c65ecee820dd58f5/docs/troubleshooting/installation.md)
guide.
